classification.difficultyReason: Combine two general-term exponents with different step sizes, solve the bounded index-pair equation and add both coefficient contributions.

content.prompt:
Find the coefficient of $x^{12}$ in the expansion of
$$\left(x-\frac{3}{x}\right)^4\left(2x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^6.$$

answer.short:
$3648$

Match the general terms with $k+2r=2$ and add their coefficients.
answer.worked:
The products of general terms have the form
$$\begin{align*}T_{k,r}&=\binom{4}{k}x^{4-k}\left(-\frac{3}{x}\right)^k\binom{6}{r}(2x^2)^{6-r}\left(\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^r\\T_{k,r}&=\binom{4}{k}\binom{6}{r}(-3)^k2^{6-r}x^{16-2k-4r}.\end{align*}$$
The power is $12$ when
$$\begin{align*}16-2k-4r&=12\\k+2r&=2.\end{align*}$$
The valid pairs are $(k,r)=(2,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\text{Coefficient of }x^{12}&=\binom{4}{2}\binom{6}{0}(-3)^2 2^6+\binom{4}{0}\binom{6}{1}(-3)^0 2^5\\\text{Coefficient of }x^{12}&=3456+192\\\text{Coefficient of }x^{12}&=3648.\end{align*}$$
